_readme: Sherpa-onnx detects enabled phrases from this manifest using English phone tokens from the bundled zh-en KWS model.
To add or change a phrase, edit id/phrase/enabled here, then run: python3 tool/generate_wake_keywords.py

Sensitivity is 0.0 to 1.0. The app maps it to sherpa keyword score 1.0 to 3.0 and threshold 0.35 to 0.15; score/threshold may override that mapping per phrase when a measured trade-off needs to stay explicit.
The Settings 'Wake sensitivity' choice (Normal/High) shifts every phrase's score/threshold and the wake input gain; those numbers live in lib/core/wake/wake_tuning.dart, not here.
"requires": "wake_on_greetings" keeps a phrase out of the detector unless the driver turned on Settings > Wake on greetings.
Use a lowercase snake_case id without spaces. Token generation fails if a word is absent from the model's English phone lexicon.
Kora and Cora have identical phone tokens in the bundled lexicon, so the Cora phrases are the same detector as the Kora phrases; the engine sends one line per distinct token sequence.
Multi-word phrases are safer in road and cab noise. Bare Kora is enabled so the product name works as a wake phrase; monitor device false accepts.

phrases.note: Primary keyword with conservative tuning. Synthetic Cora samples are indistinguishable from Kora, so Cora is accepted too; phone false-accept testing is required.
Same phones as Kora in this model, so it shares Kora's detector and tuning.
Casual greeting; enable after device testing.
Bare greeting. Only listened for when Settings > Wake on greetings is on; it also fires on ordinary conversation.
The phrase consumes the help intent, so Kora should ask what is needed.
Add a phrase here, then regenerate keywords.txt.
